simulation.description: DTMF dual-tone signal generation and sampling simulation

expected_behavior: The time-domain signal should contain two sinusoidal components at 770 Hz and 1336 Hz.
The FFT should contain dominant peaks near 770 Hz and 1336 Hz.
No significant frequency components should exist outside the two dominant DTMF tones.
The sampling frequency of 8000 Hz provides a Nyquist frequency of 4000 Hz.
The Zero-Order Hold represents the sampling/channel stage.
graph_descriptions: dtmf_time_domain_770Hz_1336Hz.png: Zoomed time-domain view of the first 30 ms of the DTMF signal. The waveform is the sum of two sinusoidal signals at 770 Hz and 1336 Hz.
dtmf_complete_signal_770Hz_1336Hz.png: Complete time-domain simulation lasting 0.250 seconds. Shows the entire sampled DTMF waveform.
dtmf_frequency_spectrum_770Hz_1336Hz.png: FFT spectrum from 0 to 2000 Hz. The two dominant components should occur at approximately 770 Hz and 1336 Hz.
dtmf_frequency_components_770Hz_1336Hz.png: Zoomed FFT spectrum from 500 to 1600 Hz, focusing on the expected DTMF frequency components at 770 Hz and 1336 Hz.
analysis_notes: The spectrum should show two dominant peaks corresponding to the DTMF tones.
Additional significant peaks may indicate distortion, spectral leakage, numerical artifacts, or unintended signal components.
